nodes.description: TellorStorage.TellorStorageStruct instance holding all protocol storage (uintVars, addressVars, disputes, balances, staking info).
Constant address of the new Tellor implementation that becomes the delegatecall target after transition.
Constant address of the legacy Tellor implementation used as delegatecall target before transition.
Internal one-time migration that rewrites timeTarget, difficulty, version and sets tellorContract to newTellor.
Internal view that returns true only when slotProgress == 0, i.e. no mining round is in progress.
Payable fallback function that optionally runs the transition then delegatecalls the forwarded msg.data to the chosen Tellor address.
Assembly delegatecall executing untrusted bytecode of the target Tellor contract in this contract's storage context with raw msg.data.
Local variable holding the delegatecall target address, initially currentTellor and switched to newTellor after the transition.
Local bytes copy of msg.data forwarded verbatim as the delegatecall calldata payload.

edges.reason: _transition writes tellor.uintVars/timeTarget, difficulty, version and tellor.addressVars/tellorContract inside the shared Tellor storage struct.
_transition reads the newTellor constant and stores it as tellor.addressVars[keccak256("tellorContract")].
The fallback function calls _isReady() to decide whether the migration should be executed.
If _isReady() returns true the fallback function invokes _transition() before delegating the call.
_isReady reads tellor.uintVars[keccak256("slotProgress")] from the Tellor storage struct.
The fallback function reaches the assembly delegatecall after the readiness check and optional transition.
The local addr variable supplies the target address argument of the delegatecall.
The local _calldata buffer supplies the calldata pointer/length arguments of the delegatecall.
addr is initialised from the currentTellor constant before the readiness check.
addr is reassigned to the newTellor constant when the transition has been performed.
The delegatecall executes the target contract's untrusted code inside this contract, which can re-enter the fallback/entrypoint or mutate state before the original frame completes.
Because delegatecall runs in this contract's context, the delegated code can arbitrarily read and write the tellor storage struct (uintVars, addressVars, disputes, balances).

normalization_plan.reason: The local addr only exists to select the delegatecall target (currentTellor or newTellor), so it is folded into the core unsafe delegatecall operation node.
The local _calldata is merely the msg.data buffer passed straight to the delegatecall, so it is folded into the core unsafe delegatecall operation node.
